functions.name: main / run
functions.signature: fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode  // thin wrapper over run(agent:&str, event:&str, stdin:&str)->io::Result<()>
functions.behavior: Top-level dispatcher replacing the whole script body (agent-hook.sh:10-19,36-45,131-163). argv[1]=agent (required), argv[2]=event (default "start"). Reads ALL of stdin into a String. Parses payload once. Derives session_id (slash-sanitised); if empty, exit 0 silently. Applies the copilot-recoverable error remap. Then branches: event=="end" -> end_session and exit; "working" -> ensure_registered + guard + mark_working; "needsAttention" -> ensure_registered + guard + mark_attention; ANY OTHER value (incl. "start") -> register_session (full re-register). Always exit 0 on the normal paths.
functions.side_effects: Reads stdin, env (TMUX_PANE, XDG_STATE_HOME/HOME, PWD), spawns `ps` (ancestry), creates dirs + writes/removes files under the state dir.
edge_cases: Missing agent arg: script uses ${1:?} which prints an error and exits non-zero under set -e — Rust must error/exit non-zero, NOT default it.
Missing event arg defaults to "start" (event=${2:-start}).

event="error" is remapped BEFORE any branch: agent=="copilot" AND recoverable==Some(true) -> "working", else -> "needsAttention". Non-copilot error, copilot non-recoverable, and copilot recoverable-missing all -> needsAttention.
Unknown/unhandled event strings fall through to the final register_session (default arm), NOT a no-op — this is the else of the if-chain (agent-hook.sh:162).
Empty session_id -> exit 0 with no side effects (agent-hook.sh:36).
set -euo pipefail: the only place pipefail could bite (the parse pipeline) is defused with `2>/dev/null || true`; Rust parse errors must be swallowed the same way (treated as empty payload).
'end' removes registry + attention + working unconditionally and exits even if the session was never registered (rm -f is non-failing).

functions.name: parse_payload
functions.signature: fn parse_payload(stdin: &str) -> Payload  // Payload { session_id_raw:String, cwd:String, transcript:String, recoverable:Option<bool>, attention_token:u128 }
functions.behavior: Replaces the inline python (agent-hook.sh:21-32). Parse stdin as one JSON object. Extract with snake_case-first, camelCase-fallback: session_id = session_id ?? sessionId ?? ""; transcript = transcript_path ?? transcriptPath ?? ""; cwd = cwd ?? "". recoverable: JSON true->Some(true), false->Some(false), missing/null/other->None. attention_token = current time in nanoseconds (python time.time_ns(); wall-clock ns since epoch), computed on EVERY invocation regardless of event.
functions.side_effects: Reads the system clock (attention_token). No I/O.
edge_cases: Invalid/empty/non-object JSON: python catch-all makes the whole parsed block empty -> every field empty, recoverable None; must NOT panic. Return an empty Payload.

attention_token is time.time_ns() = wall-clock nanoseconds, NOT a monotonic clock — must use SystemTime::now() duration since UNIX_EPOCH as_nanos (u128), so tokens stay comparable to any previously written marker across process restarts. Do not substitute Instant.
recoverable is a tri-state; only the exact JSON boolean true (from copilot) yields Some(true). A string "true" in JSON is NOT true (python checks `is True`).
session_id/transcript accept only the two documented key spellings each; no other aliases.
The payload is read even for events that never use cwd/transcript/token (e.g. working) — parsing is unconditional and errors are non-fatal.

functions.name: sanitize_session_id
functions.behavior: Replace EVERY '/' with '_' (bash ${session_id//\//_}, agent-hook.sh:35). Used to build the registry/marker filename component; must match byte-for-byte so files land where assoc/notify/rows look.
edge_cases: Global replace, all slashes, not just the first.
No other characters are sanitised (spaces, backslashes, etc. pass through verbatim) — replicate exactly, do not add extra escaping.

functions.name: record_key / paths
functions.signature: fn record_key(agent:&str, session_id:&str) -> String  // format!("{agent}-{session_id}"); plus state_dir(), registry_path(), attention_path(), working_path()
functions.behavior: Filename key is literally `${agent}-${session_id}` (agent-hook.sh:85 etc.). state_dir() = ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/tmux-agent-wrangler (agent-hook.sh:12, matches sidebar.py:34-40). REGISTRY=<state>/sessions, ATTENTION=<state>/attention, WORKING=<state>/working. Each marker/record file for a session shares the identical key.
edge_cases: The single '-' separator between agent and session_id is significant: the reader splits it back off with startswith(agent+"-") (sidebar.py:449-450). An agent name containing '-' would be fine on write but the reader strips only the leading `agent-` prefix; keep agent names as the manifest defines (claude, copilot).
XDG_STATE_HOME empty vs unset: bash ${VAR:-default} treats empty the SAME as unset (falls back). Rust env::var returns Ok("") for empty — must treat empty as fallback too.
HOME fallback path is $HOME/.local/state; do not hardcode a different base.

functions.name: find_agent_pid
functions.behavior: Walk process ancestry from the hook's own PID upward to find the agent process, so the sidebar can prune the record if the end hook is skipped (agent-hook.sh:67-82). Start pid = getpid(). Up to 8 iterations: pid = ppid(pid) via `ps -o ppid= -p <pid>`; stop if empty or <=1; read cmdline via `ps -o command= -p <pid>`; if cmdline contains "agent-hook" (case-sensitive substring) skip this level (continue climbing); else if cmdline contains the agent name case-INSENSITIVELY, return that pid. Return None if not found within 8 levels.
functions.side_effects: Spawns `ps` up to ~16 times. Reads own PID.
edge_cases: Bounded to exactly 8 ancestry hops — replicate the cap; do not walk to init unbounded.
Break condition is ppid empty OR ppid <= 1 (stops at init/pid1).
The agent-hook skip test is literal substring "agent-hook" and is CASE-SENSITIVE (bash case glob *agent-hook*); the agent-name match is CASE-INSENSITIVE (grep -qi).
On `continue` (agent-hook match) the loop STILL advances because the next iteration recomputes pid from its ppid — it keeps climbing, does not stall.

agent is used as a grep BRE pattern; "claude"/"copilot" have no regex metacharacters so a plain case-insensitive substring match is faithful. If future agent names carried metacharacters this would diverge — treat as literal substring for parity with current names.

Uses `ps` ancestry (not /proc, not controlling tty) deliberately for macOS+Linux parity — a Rust /proc-only implementation would break macOS; prefer invoking `ps` or a cross-platform ancestry that yields identical results.
Not found -> pid field written empty; the reader then cannot prune-by-pid and only prunes-by-pane (sidebar.py:439,446).

functions.name: register_session
functions.behavior: Write (overwrite) the 5-field registry record (agent-hook.sh:57-86). Fields, tab-separated, trailing newline: pane\tagent\tpid\tcwd\ttranscript. pane = TMUX_PANE or empty. pid = find_agent_pid() or empty. cwd = payload.cwd or (if empty) current process working dir ($PWD). transcript = payload.transcript (may be empty). mkdir -p REGISTRY first.
functions.side_effects: Creates REGISTRY dir; runs the ancestry walk (ps); writes REGISTRY/<key>.
edge_cases: CRITICAL PARITY: there is NO TMUX_PANE guard here. The script writes a record even outside tmux, recording an EMPTY pane field (this is exactly how daemon-hosted / pane-less Claude sessions register). CLAUDE.md's claim that register_session is a no-op outside tmux is NOT what this file does — do not add such a guard.

Empty pane field is intentional and load-bearing: the reader files an empty-pane record under the Agents group and never prunes it for pane reasons. Must write a genuinely empty field (leading tab), preserved on read via rstrip('\n') only (sidebar.py:424-428).
cwd fallback is the hook process's own working directory (bash $PWD), used only when payload cwd is empty.
transcript may legitimately be empty (daemon record) — write it as an empty trailing field; the record still has 5 fields (the final \t then newline).
This is the ONLY path that runs the ancestry walk; start and unknown events call it directly, working/needsAttention reach it only via ensure_registered when the record is absent.

Writes are not atomic in the original (plain > redirect / truncate); a concurrent reader could see a partial line, but parity does not require atomicity — matching field layout matters more. (An atomic write is a safe improvement but keep the exact bytes.)

functions.name: read_record
functions.signature: fn read_record(path:&Path) -> Option<[String;5]>  // pane, agent, pid, cwd, transcript
functions.behavior: Read the first line of an existing record, splitting on TAB into 5 fields WITHOUT trimming empties (agent-hook.sh:104-109 uses `cut -f1..5`, explicitly NOT `IFS=$'\t' read`). Preserves an empty leading pane field.
edge_cases: MUST NOT use a whitespace-splitting/trimming reader: the comment (agent-hook.sh:100-103) warns that tab-as-IFS trims the empty leading pane field and shifts every field left, corrupting a pane-less record so the sidebar prunes it. Split on '\t' with fixed field positions, empties kept.
Only the FIRST line is read (bash `read -r line`).

cut -fN on a line with fewer fields yields empty for the missing ones — a legacy 2-field record (pane\tcwd) read here gives old_agent=cwd, old_pid/old_transcript empty. refresh_record can therefore mangle a legacy record, but in practice legacy records lack a transcript so refresh is a no-op (see refresh_record edge cases).
Trailing newline is stripped; embedded tabs in a field are impossible by construction (fields are pane/agent/pid/cwd/transcript, none contains a tab from the writer).

functions.name: refresh_record
functions.behavior: Update an existing record's cwd+transcript IN PLACE when the payload carries a transcript path that differs from the stored one, preserving pane/agent/pid (agent-hook.sh:88-115). If payload.transcript empty -> return (nothing to refresh). Read existing record; if payload.transcript == old_transcript -> return (unchanged). Else rewrite: old_pane\told_agent\told_pid\t(cwd?:old_cwd)\tnew_transcript. cwd = payload.cwd or old_cwd if payload cwd empty.
edge_cases: Guarded by non-empty transcript: a payload with no transcript never refreshes (so high-frequency turn events on daemon/no-transcript sessions are cheap no-ops).
Preserves pane and pid deliberately (skips the ancestry walk) — a relocated session keeps its identity, only cwd/transcript move. Do not recompute pid here.
Purpose is the worktree/relocation case: same session_id, transcript path moves to a new project dir; without this the sidebar would read title/color from a stale path (agent-hook.sh:90-94).
If read_record fails (missing file / open error) the bash `|| return 0` makes it a silent no-op — but ensure_registered only calls refresh when the file exists, so this is defensive.

On a legacy 2-field record old_transcript is empty; if the payload has a transcript it differs, so refresh WOULD fire and rewrite using old_agent=<the cwd> — a latent corruption. Preserve current behavior (do not special-case), but note it as a legacy quirk; it is unreachable for records written by this hook (always 5-field).

functions.name: ensure_registered
functions.behavior: If REGISTRY/<key> exists -> refresh_record; else -> register_session (agent-hook.sh:123-129). Makes every turn event self-healing: a session whose start hook was missed (notably a resumed Claude session) reappears on the next event, and a relocated transcript is picked up.
functions.side_effects: May write the record (via either branch).
edge_cases: Existence check is on the registry file only; markers are not consulted.
Registration cost (ancestry walk) is paid once at first appearance, not per high-frequency event — the exists->refresh branch is the fast path.
There is a TOCTOU between the exists check and the write, benign in the original (rare, files converge).

functions.name: mark_working
functions.behavior: ensure_registered, then the post-ensure guard (re-check REGISTRY/<key> exists; if not, exit 0), then mkdir -p WORKING, TRUNCATE/create an EMPTY file WORKING/<key>, and rm -f ATTENTION/<key> (agent-hook.sh:142-149). Establishes the working half of the mutually-exclusive turn state.
functions.side_effects: Creates WORKING dir + empty marker; deletes attention marker.
edge_cases: Post-ensure guard: if registration left no record (e.g. state dir uncreatable), skip the marker entirely and exit 0 — do NOT write a marker for an unregistered session (avoids orphan markers).
Working marker CONTENT is empty (bash `: >` truncation); only its existence matters to the reader (sidebar.py:494 os.path.exists).
Mutual exclusion: writing working MUST delete attention in the same call; the two markers must never both exist for one key (invariant the reader relies on to pick status).
rm -f is non-failing when attention marker is absent.

functions.name: mark_attention
functions.behavior: ensure_registered, post-ensure guard, mkdir -p ATTENTION, write the attention_token as a single line (token + '\n') to ATTENTION/<key>, and rm -f WORKING/<key> (agent-hook.sh:152-159). Establishes the attention half of the turn state.
functions.side_effects: Creates ATTENTION dir + token marker; deletes working marker.
edge_cases: Attention marker CONTENT is the nanosecond event token (unlike the empty working marker). notify/assoc read this token (_attention_token) to fire exactly one signal per distinct event and to gate focus-acknowledge clearing (sidebar.py:354,492,530-541). An empty attention marker is treated as a legacy valid marker by the reader, so writing the token is important but a missing token must not crash consumers.
Token is written verbatim as printed by python (decimal integer, no leading zeros); Rust must format u128 decimal identically so string comparisons in the reader match.
Same post-ensure guard and mutual-exclusion delete-of-working as mark_working.
Each needsAttention invocation writes a NEW token (fresh time.time_ns()), so re-attention overwrites with a strictly increasing value — the monotonic-ish ordering the notify dedup depends on.

functions.name: end_session
functions.behavior: rm -f REGISTRY/<key>, ATTENTION/<key>, WORKING/<key> then exit 0 (agent-hook.sh:131-134). Full teardown, no registration first.
edge_cases: Non-failing removal (rm -f semantics): missing files are fine; never error if the session was never registered.
Does NOT touch the notified/ flag (that is owned by the sidebar's notify path, not the hook) — do not delete it here.
end takes precedence: it is checked before the turn-state branches (agent-hook.sh:131).

functions.name: manifest event->action mapping (glue-owned data, referenced by hook)
functions.signature: // data contract, not a hook fn: hooks-manifest.json consumed by install-hooks (glue)
functions.behavior: hooks-manifest.json encodes the agent-native-event -> hook-action state machine (working/needsAttention/start/end/error) plus matchers. The HOST agent (Claude/Copilot) applies matchers and invokes agent-hook.sh with the already-resolved action string; agent-hook.sh does NO matching itself.
edge_cases: Matchers (PreToolUse AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode; Copilot notification shell_completed|... and permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog) are enforced by the agent, not the hook — the Rust hook binary receives the resolved action and must NOT re-implement matching.
The ONLY runtime action-derivation the hook does is the copilot-recoverable error remap; every other event arrives pre-mapped to start/end/working/needsAttention.
Copilot subagentStart/subagentStop both map to "working" (subagents keep the parent working, never create their own row).
Copilot notification's shell/agent completion+idle matchers map to working; permission/elicitation map to needsAttention.

Claude Notification idle_prompt/elicitation_dialog -> needsAttention; Claude Stop/StopFailure/PermissionRequest -> needsAttention; PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/PostToolBatch/SubagentStart/UserPromptSubmit -> working.

If the Rust port keeps agent-hook.sh's `<agent> <action>` CLI contract, install-hooks/glue and the manifest need no change; if it changes the CLI, the manifest renderer (glue) must change in lockstep.

side_effects: The hook is almost entirely side effects: reads stdin + env (TMUX_PANE, XDG_STATE_HOME/HOME, PWD, own PID), spawns `ps` for the ancestry walk, and mutates the shared state dir (~/.local/state/tmux-agent-wrangler): creates sessions/, working/, attention/ dirs and writes/removes per-session files keyed `<agent>-<sanitised session_id>`. It never touches notified/, selection, or width. It emits no bell/notification (the sidebar does). Output must be byte-compatible with the readers in assoc/notify/rows.
parity_risks: attention_token is wall-clock nanoseconds (time.time_ns()), NOT monotonic — use SystemTime since UNIX_EPOCH as u128 nanos and format as plain decimal; the notify dedup compares these tokens as strings/ints across processes, so formatting and clock source must match.
NO TMUX_PANE guard on registration: the real script writes a record (empty pane field) even outside tmux; CLAUDE.md's 'no-op outside tmux' description is inaccurate for THIS file. Do not add a guard.

Empty leading pane field must be preserved on both write and read. The record is split by TAB with FIXED positions (cut), never by whitespace/trim — a trimming reader shifts fields left and the sidebar prunes the record. Read strips only the trailing newline.
5-field record layout pane\tagent\tpid\tcwd\ttranscript with a genuine trailing empty transcript field (line ends \t\n) for daemon records.

Legacy 2-field record format (pane\tcwd from old claude-hook.sh) is a READ concern the sidebar still honors (sidebar.py:431); the hook always writes 5-field. refresh_record on a legacy record would corrupt it, but is unreachable for hook-written records (they always carry a transcript-or-empty 5-field shape).

Ancestry walk is bounded to 8 hops, stops at ppid<=1, skips cmdlines containing 'agent-hook' (case-SENSITIVE) and matches the agent name case-INSENSITIVELY — replicate all three exactly; an unbounded or /proc-only walk breaks parity/macOS.
Mutual-exclusion invariant: working and attention markers must never coexist for one key; every mark_* deletes the other's marker. Preserve this atomic pairing.
Working marker is EMPTY; attention marker CONTAINS the token — different content semantics for two same-shaped files.
Post-ensure guard: skip writing a marker if registration left no record (state dir uncreatable) — prevents orphan markers.
Unknown/unrecognised event strings fall through to a full register_session (default arm), not a no-op.
copilot-recoverable error remap: only agent=='copilot' AND JSON recoverable===true -> working; everything else (non-copilot, non-recoverable, missing recoverable) -> needsAttention.
session_id slash-to-underscore is a GLOBAL replace; the filename key is `<agent>-<session_id>` and the reader strips exactly the `<agent>-` prefix.

JSON key spellings: session_id/sessionId, transcript_path/transcriptPath, cwd, recoverable — snake_case tried first; unknown/missing -> empty/None; parse failure must be swallowed (yields empty payload, then exit 0), never panic.
cwd fallback differs by path: register_session falls back to the hook's own PWD; refresh_record falls back to the stored old_cwd.
'end' does not delete the notified/ flag and is checked before turn-state branches.
Matchers live in the host-agent config (rendered from the manifest by glue), NOT in the hook — the hook must not re-implement matcher regexes.
XDG_STATE_HOME empty string must be treated as unset (fall back to $HOME/.local/state), matching bash ${VAR:-default}.
